summary: Backend (7/7 pytest) and Frontend E2E of Page SEO, Popup, and responsiveness completed. Backend endpoints /api/seo/pages and /api/popup all working (GET public, PUT auth-protected, persistence verified, About restore verified). Popup end-to-end works perfectly: 5 admin tabs render, popup panel saves & persists, popup appears on public site at 390px & 1920px, close (X) sets ml_lead_popup_seen and prevents reappear on reload, form submits create enquiry with product 'Website Popup Enquiry' visible in admin. CRITICAL BUG FOUND: per-page SEO override (useManagedPageSeo) is NOT applied on any static route on the public site — all static pages (/, /products, /about, /contact, /gallery, /industries, /why-choose-us, /faq) show the SAME global title from /api/seo. Only dynamic pages using usePageSeo (product detail, /market-areas) apply their own SEO. Root cause: race condition in /app/frontend/src/hooks/useSeoSettings.js — useSeoSettings() and useManagedPageSeo() both run in Layout as parallel async fetches; whichever resolves LAST wins because both call applySeo() unconditionally when !pageActive. The /api/seo defaults response almost always resolves after /api/seo/pages and overwrites the per-page title.

integration_issues.issue: useManagedPageSeo is defeated by useSeoSettings loading defaults after it — final document.title on /, /products, /about, /contact, /gallery, /industries, /why-choose-us, /faq is the GLOBAL site title, not the page-specific one saved in admin. Verified via network trace: both /api/seo and /api/seo/pages return 200 but defaults overwrites. Titles are only 2 unique across 9 pages (only /market-areas differs, because it uses usePageSeo directly).

action_items: Fix race condition in /app/frontend/src/hooks/useSeoSettings.js so per-page SEO wins over global defaults. Options: (a) inside loadDefaults, do NOT overwrite document.title if a page-level title has already been applied (track a `pageManagedApplied` flag similar to pageActive), or (b) in useSeoSettings, only apply defaults when no page-level SEO exists for the current pathname, or (c) always apply defaults first, then re-apply page SEO on every render/pathname change after both promises settle (Promise.all).
After fix, retest by loading /, /about, /contact etc. and confirming document.title matches values shown in admin > Page SEO tab.
Also invalidate the module-level pageSeoMap cache after admin saves (currently a user must full-reload to see saved changes on the public site since map is cached at module scope).
critical_code_review_comments: useSeoSettings.js: `defaults` and `pageSeoMap` are module-level singletons that never invalidate — admin edits to SEO pages will not reflect in an already-loaded SPA session; only full page reloads pick up new values.

rca of the issue: PER-PAGE SEO NOT APPLIED — Root cause: In /app/frontend/src/hooks/useSeoSettings.js, Layout.jsx calls both useSeoSettings() (loads /api/seo defaults) and useManagedPageSeo(pathname) (loads /api/seo/pages). Both are async fetches. Each side calls applySeo() which sets document.title. There is no ordering guarantee — the defaults fetch (/api/seo) typically finishes AFTER the pages fetch (/api/seo/pages) and calls applySeo(data) with the global site_title, overwriting the page-specific one. The pageActive flag is only set by usePageSeo (dynamic detail pages), so static routes remain vulnerable. Reproduction: navigate to https://print-shop-test.preview.emergentagent.com/about → document.title == 'My Labels UAE | Printing, Labels & Apparel — Dubai, Al Ain, Fujairah, RAK' instead of the per-page title stored in /api/seo/pages. Fix: introduce a second flag e.g. `managedApplied` set inside useManagedPageSeo after applySeo, and in loadDefaults/applySeo skip document.title / description overwrite when managedApplied is true; and re-apply managed SEO on pathname change and after defaults resolves.
